Sure thing—Let us begin our simple yet crucial planting guide on sown flower bulbs in your own backyard:

**Select a Sunny, Shelter-Spot**

Start off finding just that ideal spot where you plan to dig in, and it should have a generous helping dose or direct sunshine. Most bulb types thrive with a daily sunlight dose between about six to ten solid and shining moments per day for optimal flowering. However a few will appreciate morning sunshine but can manage some afternoon shelter, like a partial shadow or duff shade, depending.

Choose this spot also by checking that you won not accidentally bury utility pipes. It can help by gently probing and poking a meter or so into ground before digging in earnest for a full picture.

Once you locate an appropriate sunspot for these beaut, ensure its not near trees with roots who would love a chance for an extra helping to grow at your plant. Trees compete fiercely with bulbs. Their roots and roots’ roots (or lateral roots to give them an actual term, if we're in the right botanical mood for a term or so here), will gladly reach and steal all water or food from your new plants before these ever have much time
